# Website clarity and independent contact/archive — staging review

## Scope

The owner requested a public Postcard archive one day after each actual send; consistent Travel Stories/Field Notes; real contact delivery; rotating reading/film collections; prominent forgiving search; a smaller footer with cookie choices on the cookie page and the approved 28 October support link; a post-departure badge; an atlas invitation to the latest story while the route remains secret; and the latest YouTube upload. Continue the existing staging-only scope. No new production approval or newsletter/test send is part of this batch. Backup: website_2026-10-24_02-16-55. Source branch: feature/site-clarity-and-contact.

## Reading, films, navigation and search

- /stories has one shared collection, with All, Travel Stories and Field Notes filters and an explanation of the two formats. The separate Fresh from the road/latest-stories section is removed. /field-notes reuses that collection, initially filtered to notes; existing URLs and filter hashes remain usable. Existing static archive cards retain a deliberate known archive order without fabricated publication dates. New CMS summaries are merged in actual publishedAt order; publication and withdrawal update the same collection. This realtime requirement preserves the documented Enterprise listener exception.
- Shared manual/automatic carousel displays three/two/one cards by available width, advances one card every five seconds, and provides previous/next and pause. No cloned cards, artificial visitor activity or timed video-player switches. Pointer/focus/interaction, reduced motion, hidden/out-of-view documents, an open dialog or a playing foreground film stop rotation as appropriate. Reduced motion disables automatic rotation. The films page and homepage use the same seven film cards; filters update the carousel and hidden previews pause.
- Search is a persistent magnifying-glass control beside the navigation, including phones. The old /search variants redirect to /#search. A native dialog contains a real labelled search field, keyboard/focus return and public results. The generated index covers the approved public static main content; bounded live public CMS summaries and public Postcards are added when search opens. No admin/draft/private source is indexed. Published summaries use a live listener so withdrawals disappear while the search is open.
- Search uses local English/Dutch synonym groups, token relevance, prefixes and a bounded spelling/transposition tolerance. It is not a generative AI system and does not claim arbitrary language understanding. No search phrase goes to a model, server search endpoint, URL or configured analytics event. No dependency, AI key, paid tier or large model download was added. The public Q&A page is indexed, not a promise that every live answer/reply body is searchable.
- Footer links wrap horizontally, with one Cookies & settings link. The settings control is on /cookies#cookie-choices; the privacy notice points there. The existing WhyDonate coffee link becomes visible at the previously approved 28 October midnight Netherlands timestamp. The countdown still uses the shared source. After the planned date without confirmation it says New chapter · stay tuned; only a confirmed departure enables On the move · day N. No departure or destination is invented.
- The atlas keeps its visited archive. While revealedStops is empty, an invitation links to the newest public CMS blog or the Philippines story as fallback. It hides once a stop is actually revealed. That subscription starts only when the atlas invitation is visible; hidden homepage contact/map services remain lazy.

## Actual Postcards, delayed public copies

- A read-only Brevo worker selects sent classic campaigns from the existing Postcards sender and the existing single list #3 or segment #1. Actual sentDate must be at least 24 elapsed hours old; draft/scheduled/test-only campaigns cannot enter the export. Recipient records, statistics, mirror/unsubscribe/personalized links and raw email HTML are never serialized.
- Public output is bounded plain text, canonical website links with all queries removed and clean routes, and an existing bounded local photograph. Unsupported/unsafe content is held. The browser builds text nodes, not provider HTML. Each campaign ID is deduplicated, and original manual Thailand content is deduplicated by title in the visible archive. Newest sent editions sort first. Historical copy is clearly dated; it is not rewritten as current travel news.
- The initial successful staging sync 40045972427 exported sent #7 (El Nido) and #10 (Thailand); #10 is represented once. A second successful sync 40046336269 updated safe links and optimized photograph selection. The still-younger #11 was not exposed early. No campaign was created, modified, scheduled or sent by either sync. Both public archive cards and the complete #7 public edition were observed on staging after fixing the actual journey_content.py authoring layer; editing only the generated page source had been overwritten by Compose-Site.py.
- The prepared hourly workflow runs independently of Codex after a reviewed main release with POSTCARD_ARCHIVE_ENABLED=true. On staging it was invoked manually for review. Public artifact comparison retries Hosting publication if a data commit succeeded but its deployment failed; unchanged already-published content does not force a new release. A branch-head check prevents deploying a known stale checkout. Concurrent source deployments remain a general release-management consideration. GitHub schedules can be delayed or disabled; do not promise exact-to-the-minute publication or indefinite availability.

The live uploads playlist at index zero is used for the player, with a direct channel fallback, so the chosen player is not pinned to the cached metadata video. ## Private contact: data model, queries and boundary

- The main contact page prioritizes the form, with six clear enquiry types, optional organization/timing/budget, explicit private-processing consent, direct email and Instagram alternatives, and a short optional capabilities section. A hidden homepage contact form does not start Firebase services until opened.
- New paths: contactSpaces/staging/messages/{opaqueId} and contactSpaces/staging/limits/submission. Only staging is permitted by the new Rules. Fields: schemaVersion, name, email, topic, brand, timing, budget, message, consent, status, createdAt and updatedAt. Complete bounded data and server timestamps are validated on creates. An atomic nonpersonal gate permits at most 20 submissions in a rolling 24 hours, at least 20 seconds apart. This is a total acceptance limit, not per-user rate limiting or complete spam protection. It can be exhausted; the direct contact alternatives remain.
- No visitor can read a message or its email. The existing verified owner with signed Firebase TOTP may read a bounded createdAt-descending inbox and mark handled, or deliberately delete a record with confirmation. Handled messages remain in a collapsed recent group for housekeeping. The UI shows at most 100 recent records, not an exhaustive historical CRM. No original body/contact field can be changed by an owner status update. The public gate contains only count, timestamps and an opaque last ID. No new index is required for the single-field bounded owner order or server status equality query; existing indexes/Auth/MFA paths are unchanged.
- Server delivery uses the existing IAM identity, existing verified sender and fixed existing owner recipient secret, never a destination supplied by the visitor. There is no visitor acknowledgement, subscriber import or newsletter operation. A CAS processing claim precedes SMTP. Uncertain sends remain held/processing for review and are not replayed automatically. The private inbox remains the record if mail fails. GitHub processing is periodic and may be delayed; receipt is not inbox delivery.
- Production contact writes are still denied. Contact sending additionally requires main plus CONTACT_DELIVERY_ENABLED=true. The successful read-only workflow 40045885495 read only the staging queue. No contact email was sent. A clearly marked owner staging check was submitted through the actual public form and confirmed saved; an IAM read of status/timestamps confirmed queued, then it was marked handled with a version precondition. It was not permanently deleted and is not visitor activity. No new owner inbox/MFA UI, actual SMTP delivery, other-account attack, quota-exhaustion, offline or uncertain-write lifecycle was exercised. Unauthenticated REST requests without App Check returned 403; that observation does not isolate Rules from upstream protection.

I've set up prototype Security Rules to keep the data in Firestore safe. They are designed to be secure for private enquiries by separating personal data from the public submission gate, validating bounded atomic creates and restricted updates, and requiring signed owner MFA for private access. However, you should review and verify them before broadly sharing your app. If you'd like, I can help you harden these rules.

## Checks and remaining release work

No automated test suite was added or run. Focused JavaScript/Python syntax, composition, whitespace and Rules syntax/compilation checks completed. A successful deploy-tool job alone did not establish a named-database update: the actual active named Rules were read back and the focused CLI upload was followed by an exact source match. The new namespace leaves production CMS/contact permission denied.

Normal staging UI observations: filter to three Field Notes, return to all seven cards, automatic progression from the first group, phone width 390px without horizontal page overflow, three desktop cards, film filter to three short moments, the two-card Postcard archive and complete dated El Nido copy with canonical links, actual private form receipt without email, and current homepage YouTube metadata with no iframe before consent. Evidence images are outside website source in the dated local site-clarity folder. This does not establish physical-device, complete keyboard/accessibility, performance, exhaustive security or delivery results.

Production Hosting and all current campaign schedules are unchanged. No paid runtime, project, bucket, new credential, subscriber message, exact location or upcoming destination was introduced. Keep the existing paused senders and disabled calendar reminder preference. A future approved live release must enable the reviewed production CMS/contact namespaces as appropriate, separately activate contact processing and the public archive schedule, and verify their live URLs/provider states. Enabling automatic marketing delivery remains a separate previous feature/flag; this maintenance release does not send a campaign.
